title: Prayer ones the soul (ch. 43)
hookLine: prayer unites the soul to God
tomorrow: how do you write a whole book without picking up a pen?

lines: A LIST INSIDE A CABINET DOOR.
cards: Inside a kitchen cabinet door, a list in a grandmother's handwriting. Names. A surgery.
A job. Somebody far from home. Some lines have a check mark beside them.
Some don't, and she still reads every one aloud each morning. Her granddaughter asks her once: if half of them never happened, why keep going? She doesn't answer right away.
Julian of Norwich has an answer, and it begins with who started the asking.

teach.h: HE IS THE GROUND OF OUR ASKING.
teach.b: First, the start. In chapter forty-one, Julian hears our Lord say that he is the ground of our asking. First it's his will that we have something; then he makes us want it; then he makes us ask.
So prayer doesn't begin with us talking God into anything. It begins with him. Second, the dry days.
She is told to pray inwardly even when it seems to have no taste at all, because that prayer is still welcome to him. Third, the line that names today.

teach.h: PRAYER ONES THE SOUL TO GOD.
teach.b: In chapter forty-three she says prayer ones the soul to God. Ones is her old word for makes one. Her reasoning: the soul is always like God in its nature, but often unlike him in its condition, through sin.
Prayer makes it like him again, wanting what he wants. Fourth, back to the cabinet.
On Julian's reading, that list isn't a vending machine with a broken slot.
Saying those names every morning does its main work whether the check marks come or not: it keeps the one praying close to God, of one will with him.
Catholics don't stop asking for things; in the Gospels Jesus tells his followers to ask. But for Julian, asking is a road, and the place it leads is oneness.

how: Catholics pray both by asking (intercession and petition) and by simply resting with God; Julian's chapters on prayer are read as a guide to keeping on when prayer feels dry.

games.q: what does “prayer ones the soul” mean?
o: Julian's teaching that prayer makes the soul one with God
a belief that one prayer counts for the whole family
a rule that prayers must be said once a day, alone

games.q: prayer ones the soul — tap the pairs.
p: he is the ground of our asking
Julian's old word for makes one
prayer makes the soul like God

s: prayer is mainly a way to get God to change his mind
Julian hears that the asking starts with God; prayer's work is making the soul one with him.
Julian hears that God is the ground of our asking
first he wills it, then he makes us want it, then he makes us ask.
Julian says prayer that feels dry and tasteless is useless
she is told to pray inwardly even then; that prayer is still welcome.

games.q: your little brother prayed hard for a snow day. no snow, school's on, and he says prayer is broken. what would Julian tell him?
o: God only answers big, important prayers, not snow days.
pray harder tonight, and maybe it will work tomorrow.
prayer's main work is being close to God, not ordering the weather.
games.why: for Julian, prayer ones the soul to God. asking is fine; the asking is a road to being of one will with him.

practice: Close your eyes and let one thing you've been asking for come to mind. Hold it out without pushing, and let your attention move from the answer to the one you're asking.
For those who pray, the asking can become the prayer itself: to want what God wants.

wordCard.voice: Prayer ones the soul. Julian's line: prayer makes the soul one with God, of one will with him.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: prayer ones, even on the days the answer is no. Go gently.
